new_statements.rule_in_words: In Bulu, as in every Kimbe (Willaumez + Bali-Vitu) language, word stress is non-contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable; high vocoids i/u count as syllabic vowels for locating the penult.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'non-phonemic in all non-ambivalent instances' (i.e. cases where a high vocoid could be read as glide or vowel); no lexical exceptions given. For the sister language Bola, van den Berg & Wiebe 2019: 34 add antepenultimate stress when au/ai/ae/oi span the antepenult and penult and stress shift under suffixation, but that is not stated for Bulu.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level blanket statement for the seven Kimbe languages (Bali, Vitu, Bulu, Bola, Harua, Meramera, Nakanai) in a two-paragraph synchronic-phonology preamble to a comparative reconstruction; based on the author's own elicitation of word lists and texts in each language (Bulu assistant Michael Utu, n. 3). No Bulu-specific examples with stress marked.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is not Bulu-specific: Johnston 1982 states penultimate, non-phonemic stress for 'all of the Kimbe languages' (Bali, Vitu, Bulu = bulu1253, Bola = bola1250, Harua [Bola dialect], Meramera = mera1242, Nakanai = naka1262), based on his own elicitation in each, with a named Bulu assistant. The two Bola documents saved here (van den Berg & Wiebe 2019 DPPNGL 63; Bola OPD 1997/2004) describe the sister language Bola (bola1250), which the grammar explicitly treats as a language distinct from Bulu; they were the sources the bola1250 world scan named as unreachable and are now on file in this folder.

sources.note: For the sister language BOLA (bola1250), sec. 2.5 p. 34: 'Stress is not phonemic in Bola. It normally occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word, and hence stress shifts when the root is suffixed'; antepenult when au/ai/ae/oi span antepenult+penult. Sec. 1.3 treats Bulu as a separate Willaumez language and cites Rueck & Jore 2000 'Bola and Bulu Dialect Survey' (unpublished). Nothing on Bulu phonology.
